title: Merge Intervals: When Is the Crane Busy?
summary: Sort the crews' crane bookings by start, then sweep once, stretching each busy period while bookings overlap it.

analogy.scenario: Four crews book a building site's one crane for hours 4–7, 1–3, 6–9, and 12–14. The site manager wants the crane's busy periods, with overlapping bookings merged.

takeaway.summary: Sort by start; keep the last merged interval. A range that starts at or before its end overlaps it: extend the end. Otherwise start a new merged range.
whenToUse: Union of time slots, bookings, or covered stretches

scenes.narration: Four crews book the site's only crane: hours 4 to 7, 1 to 3, 6 to 9, and 12 to 14. When is the crane busy, with overlapping bookings merged into one stretch?
scenes.caption: Crane bookings 4–7, 1–3, 6–9, 12–14: when is it busy?

scenes.narration: Comparing every booking with every other one takes n squared checks, and merges can chain. Sorting by start puts overlapping bookings next to each other, so one pass is enough.
scenes.caption: Comparing every pair of bookings is O(n²)

scenes.narration: Sorted by start hour: 1 to 3, 4 to 7, 6 to 9, and 12 to 14. The busy lane at the bottom collects the merged stretches.
scenes.caption: Sorted by start: 1–3, 4–7, 6–9, 12–14

scenes.narration: The first booking, 1 to 3, opens the first busy stretch.
scenes.caption: 1–3 opens the first busy stretch

scenes.narration: Next, 4 to 7 starts at 4, after the busy stretch ends at 3. There's a gap, so it opens a new stretch.
scenes.caption: 4–7 starts at 4, after the stretch ends at 3: a new stretch

scenes.narration: Then 6 to 9 starts at 6, before the current stretch ends at 7. They overlap, so the stretch just grows to end at 9: two bookings become one busy period.
scenes.caption: 6–9 starts at 6, before 7: the stretch grows to 4–9

scenes.narration: Finally 12 to 14 starts after 9, so it opens a third stretch. The crane is busy from 1 to 3, 4 to 9, and 12 to 14.
scenes.caption: 12–14 starts after 9: busy 1–3, 4–9, 12–14

scenes.narration: Bookings are intervals. Sort by start, then each one either extends the last merged interval or starts a new one. Sorting is O(n log n), the sweep O(n).
scenes.caption: Sort by start, then extend the last merged end or start a new one
